title: Three-dimensional Global Relativistic Radiation Magnetohydrodynamics of Magnetically Arrested Disk Accretion Flows in AGNs
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We perform three-dimensional radiation-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (3D Rad-RMHD) simulations of accretion flows around spinning active galactic nuclei (AGNs). Our study focuses on the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state, adopting a single-temperature model that includes bremsstrahlung opacity as the sole radiation process while varying the black hole spin from non-spinning to rapidly spinning cases. We find that the MAD state persists across all spin values, as demonstrated by the normalized magnetic flux at the horizon and the physically motivated spatially averaged plasma beta. The overall flow dynamics remain qualitatively similar for all spin models in 3D flow, suggesting that black hole spin has minimal influence on the accretion dynamics. In addition, we conduct post-processing using a two-temperature model to calculate the luminosities from synchrotron and bremsstrahlung radiation. We find that the total radiation luminosity is significantly higher than the luminosities from synchrotron and bremsstrahlung. This finding highlights the influence of radiation on the dynamics of the accretion flow. Our analysis shows that the electron temperature is significantly high in the jet region, regardless of spin. We further find that the temporal evolution of both radiative and synchrotron luminosities exhibits qualitatively similar behavior across all spin values. Finally, our results indicate that black hole spin has minimal impact on the spectral energy distribution (SED) in MAD state accretion flows.

AI.tldr: 3D Rad-RMHD simulations of MAD state AGN accretion flows reveal that black hole spin minimally affects flow dynamics, radiation luminosity, and spectral distribution; radiation influences accretion dynamics with high jet-region electron temperatures consistent across spins.
AI.motivation: To investigate the effects of black hole spin on accretion flow dynamics and radiation properties in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states around active galactic nuclei (AGNs).
AI.method: Three-dimensional radiation-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (3D Rad-RMHD) simulations using a single-temperature model including bremsstrahlung opacity, varying black hole spin from non-spinning to rapidly spinning; post-processing with a two-temperature model to compute synchrotron and bremsstrahlung luminosities.
AI.result: MAD states persist across all spins with similar flow dynamics, showing minimal influence of black hole spin on accretion dynamics and spectral energy distribution; total radiation luminosity exceeds synchrotron and bremsstrahlung contributions; electron temperature remains high in jet regions irrespective of spin; radiative and synchrotron luminosities evolve similarly across spins.
AI.conclusion: Black hole spin exerts minimal influence on the accretion flow dynamics, radiation luminosity, and spectral energy distribution in MAD state accretion flows around AGNs, indicating that accretion properties are largely spin-independent in these scenarios.

title: Warm Inflation Beyond the Markovian Limit
summary:
Warm inflation is commonly studied under the assumption that the stochastic force sourcing inflaton fluctuations is Markovian. Realistic thermal systems, however, possess finite relaxation times and can therefore generate colored noise with non-zero correlation time. In this work, we investigate warm inflation beyond the Markovian limit and determine how finite correlation time modifies the primordial scalar power spectrum.
  We show that memory effects suppress the scalar spectrum relative to the standard white-noise result and derive a simple expression for this correction in terms of the background thermal dynamics. In particular, we relate the size of the non-Markovian effect directly to the thermal ratio between the bath temperature and the Hubble scale, thereby establishing a transparent link between warm-inflation background quantities and the validity of the Markovian approximation. We also derive the corresponding modification of the tensor-to-scalar ratio and the induced shifts in the scalar spectral index and the running of the scalar spectral index.
  Our results provide a simple and practical diagnostic for identifying when finite correlation-time effects become relevant in warm-inflation model building.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the impact of finite correlation time (non-Markovian noise) on warm inflation, showing that memory effects suppress the scalar power spectrum and modify key inflationary observables in a way controlled by thermal dynamics, thereby providing criteria to evaluate the validity of the Markovian assumption.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to go beyond the common Markovian assumption in warm inflation to understand how non-zero correlation time in thermal noise affects primordial fluctuations and inflationary predictions.
AI.method: The authors analyze warm inflation dynamics by incorporating memory effects due to finite correlation times, deriving corrections to the primordial scalar power spectrum and associated inflationary observables in terms of background thermal parameters.
AI.result: They find that memory effects suppress the scalar power spectrum compared to the Markovian white-noise case and provide a simple analytical expression for this correction linked to thermal dynamics. The study also presents modifications to the tensor-to-scalar ratio, scalar spectral index, and its running, directly tying these changes to the ratio of bath temperature to the Hubble scale.
AI.conclusion: Finite correlation-time effects introduce significant modifications to the inflationary power spectra, and their impact can be diagnosed using thermal background quantities. This offers a practical criterion for assessing when the Markovian approximation fails in warm inflation models, guiding more accurate model building.

title: Constraints on Axion-Photon Mixing from Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) offer a powerful probe of the ionized Universe through their dispersion measures (DM). While a significant fraction of the DM arises from the intergalactic medium (IGM), the contributions from the host galaxy and the immediate environment of the source remain uncertain, and the physical origin of FRBs is still under active investigation. In this work, we investigated the possibility that FRBs originate from high-magnetic-field neutron stars (NS), whose magnetospheres can facilitate axion-photon mixing. Such mixing can modify photon propagation and induce an effective contribution to the observed dispersion. Using a sample of localized FRBs with measured redshifts, we perform a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis to constrain the axion mass $m_a$ and axion-photon coupling $g_{aγγ}$. Within a parametric cosmological framework, we obtain $m_a = 1.16^{+4.40}_{-1.08}\,μ{\rm eV}$ and $g_{aγγ} = (1.76^{+6.69}_{-1.64})\times10^{-16}\,{\rm GeV}^{-1}$, together with a physically consistent intergalactic baryon fraction $f_{\rm IGM} = 0.837^{+0.053}_{-0.056}$. We further tested the robustness of our bounds against cosmological modeling assumptions by employing a non-parametric Gaussian Process reconstruction (GPR) of the DM-$z$ relation, which gives statistically consistent results.

AI.tldr: This paper uses localized FRB data and Bayesian MCMC to constrain axion parameters, proposing axion-photon mixing in neutron star magnetospheres as a potential contributor to FRB dispersion measures, yielding consistent cosmological and astrophysical constraints.
AI.motivation: To investigate the origin of FRBs and whether axion-photon mixing in neutron star magnetospheres contributes significantly to the observed dispersion measures, addressing uncertainties in host galaxy and source environment contributions.
AI.method: A Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis on a sample of localized FRBs with measured redshifts was performed, within both parametric cosmological frameworks and a non-parametric Gaussian Process reconstruction (GPR) of the DM-redshift relation.
AI.result: Constraints obtained are axion mass $m_a = 1.16^{+4.40}_{-1.08}\,μ{\rm eV}$ and coupling $g_{aγγ} = (1.76^{+6.69}_{-1.64})\times10^{-16}\,{\rm GeV}^{-1}$, along with an intergalactic baryon fraction $f_{\rm IGM} = 0.837^{+0.053}_{-0.056}$, with results robust under different cosmological modeling approaches.
AI.conclusion: The study constrains axion mass and axion-photon coupling by analyzing FRB dispersion measures, supporting the hypothesis that FRBs originate from high-magnetic-field neutron stars with axion-photon mixing in their magnetospheres.

title: SN 2023axu: A Type IIP Supernova Interacted with a Low-Density Stellar Wind1
comment: Accepted for publication in APJ, 24 pages, 16 figures
summary: We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of Type IIP supernova SN 2023axu, spanning $\sim$400 d after the explosion. Its light curve is typical of normal SNe IIP, with a V-band peak of $-17.25 \pm 0.06$ mag and no early-time excess indicative of strong circumstellar interaction. The early spectra exhibit a distinctive broad "ledge" near 4600 Å. Through spectral modeling and comparison, we attribute this feature to a blend of C, N, and He lines excited by weak interaction between the ejecta and a low-density stellar wind. The late-time photometric evolution shows no discernible contribution from interaction, arguing against strong late-time circumstellar material engagement and supporting the low-density wind scenario. From modeling, this SN synthesized $\sim 0.055\,M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni, and nebular spectrum analysis indicates a progenitor mass near $15\,M_\odot$. SN 2023axu thus exemplifies weak ejecta-wind interaction and highlights the diversity of mass-loss histories and circumstellar environments of SNe II progenitors.

AI.tldr: SN 2023axu is a typical Type IIP supernova showing weak ejecta interaction with a low-density stellar wind, synthesizing about 0.055 M☉ of nickel-56, and originating from a ~15 M☉ progenitor, highlighting diverse progenitor mass loss.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature and extent of ejecta and circumstellar matter interaction in Type IIP supernova SN 2023axu, and to understand progenitor mass-loss histories and environments by detailed photometric and spectroscopic observations.
AI.method: The study combines photometric and spectroscopic monitoring over ~400 days, spectral modeling to identify line blends near 4600 Å, comparison with known supernova spectra, photometric evolution analysis for circumstellar interaction evidence, and nebular spectrum interpretation to estimate progenitor mass and nickel-56 synthesis.
AI.result: The paper presents extensive photometric and spectroscopic data for Type IIP supernova SN 2023axu over approximately 400 days post-explosion. The observed light curve is consistent with normal Type IIP supernovae, showing no early signs of strong circumstellar interaction, such as an early-time excess. A unique broad spectral feature near 4600 Å is identified and modeled as a blend of carbon, nitrogen, and helium lines, excited by weak interaction between the ejecta and a low-density stellar wind. Later observations lack evidence for significant circumstellar interaction, supporting the interpretation of a low-density wind environment. Modeling estimates about 0.055 solar masses of nickel-56 were produced, with nebular spectra suggesting a progenitor star of approximately 15 solar masses. This study illustrates subtle ejecta-wind interactions and the varied mass-loss behavior prior to explosion in Type II SN progenitors.
AI.conclusion: SN 2023axu exhibits weak ejecta interaction with a low-density stellar wind, no significant late-time circumstellar interaction, produces ~0.055 M☉ of $^{56}$Ni, and originates from a progenitor of approximately 15 solar masses, emphasizing diversity in progenitor mass-loss histories.

title: A unified scalar-field resolution of the $H_0$, $S_8$ and evolving Dark Energy tensions
summary: We propose a unified scalar-field framework that addresses, within standard general relativity, three current cosmological anomalies: the $H_0$ tension, the mild preference for reduced late-time clustering ($S_8$), and recent indications of evolving dark energy. The model contains a single minimally coupled canonical scalar field evolving in a smooth potential composed of a localized bump superimposed on an exponential tail. The bump generates a transient pre-recombination energy injection that increases the expansion rate before last scattering, reduces the sound horizon, and shifts the CMB-inferred value of $H_0$ upward. After the field is released, its energy density rapidly redshifts through a kination-like phase, ensuring that the early modification does not persist as an unwanted late-time contribution. At low redshift, the exponential tail drives quintessence-like evolution, naturally yielding $w_0>-1$ and $w_a<0$ while suppressing linear structure growth and moving $S_8$ in the observationally preferred direction. The analysis shows explicitly how this smooth single-field potential can produce the required sequence of early enhancement, rapid dilution, and late-time thawing behavior.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a single scalar-field model with a tailored potential that reconciles tensions in cosmological measurements by modifying early expansion and late-time dark energy behavior.
AI.motivation: To address three cosmological anomalies simultaneously: the H_0 tension, reduced late-time clustering (S_8), and evolving dark energy indications.
AI.method: A unified scalar-field framework within standard general relativity using a minimally coupled canonical scalar field with a smooth potential comprising a localized bump and an exponential tail.
AI.result: The bump in the potential injects energy pre-recombination, increasing the expansion rate and raising the CMB-inferred H_0 value. The rapid redshifting of the scalar field after the bump avoids unwanted late-time effects, while the exponential tail drives quintessence-like late-time evolution, naturally adjusting dark energy parameters and suppressing structure growth to align with observations.
AI.conclusion: The smooth single-field potential can sequentially produce early expansion enhancement, rapid energy density dilution, and later-time quintessence-like evolution, thereby resolving key cosmological tensions within a unified general relativistic framework.

title: Revisiting early afterglows of gamma-ray bursts with finite-thickness ejecta: Implications from XRF 080330 and GRB 080710
summary: We revisit the physical origin of the achromatic peaks and breaks observed several thousand seconds after the burst in the multi-wavelength afterglows of XRF 080330 and GRB 080710. Using a numerical afterglow model that consistently incorporates finite ejecta thickness and a generalized external density profile, we perform Bayesian inference to estimate model parameters describing these events. Our analysis shows that the gradual rise and achromatic temporal features in both events are more naturally explained by jet dynamical evolution with finite shell thickness rather than by off-axis viewing effects. The inferred initial radial width of the ejecta is of order $10^{13}$ cm for both bursts, implying a central engine activity timescale significantly longer than that suggested by the prompt gamma-ray duration alone. Taken together, these results demonstrate that early afterglow light curves are strongly influenced by transition dynamics when finite ejecta thickness is properly taken into account, thereby providing a physical link between the prompt and afterglow phases and highlighting limitations of simply applying the thin-shell approximation when interpreting early-time afterglows. Furthermore, Bayesian model comparison favors a generalized circumburst density profile over the canonical uniform or steady-wind models, suggesting that fixing the external density structure to idealized profiles a priori may obscure crucial information about the progenitor's pre-burst activity.

AI.tldr: This study uses numerical models and Bayesian inference to show that early achromatic afterglow features in XRF 080330 and GRB 080710 arise from jet dynamics with finite ejecta thickness, linking prompt and afterglow phases, and that generalized circumburst density profiles better capture progenitor environment than standard models.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origin of achromatic peaks and breaks observed thousands of seconds after bursts in multi-wavelength afterglows, and to address the shortcomings of thin-shell approximations and fixed circumburst density profiles in early afterglow interpretation.
AI.method: Numerical afterglow modeling incorporating finite ejecta thickness and generalized external density profiles combined with Bayesian inference to estimate model parameters and perform Bayesian model comparison.
AI.result: Gradual rise and achromatic temporal features in these afterglows are more naturally explained by jet dynamics with finite shell thickness; inferred ejecta width (~10^{13} cm) suggests longer central engine activity. Bayesian comparison favors generalized density profiles over standard uniform or wind models, revealing richer progenitor information.
AI.conclusion: The achromatic peaks and breaks observed in XRF 080330 and GRB 080710 afterglows are best explained by jet dynamics with finite ejecta thickness rather than off-axis viewing, linking prompt emission to afterglow and revealing limitations of thin-shell models. Additionally, a generalized circumburst density profile better fits the data, indicating that assuming standard density profiles can mask key progenitor activity information.

title: The impact of baryons on weak lensing statistics as a function of halo mass and radius
summary: Upcoming weak lensing (WL) surveys such as those by {\it Euclid}, LSST, and {\it Roman} require percent-level control over systematic effects. A common approach to mitigating baryonic effects uses semi-analytic baryon correction models (BCMs) that modify halo profiles in dark matter-only (DMO) simulations, calibrated to statistics from hydrodynamic simulations. We investigate the limits of this approach by progressively replacing larger regions around halos of decreasing mass in DMO simulations with their hydrodynamical counterparts. We compare multiple statistics -- the matter ($P(k)$) and weak-lensing ($C_\ell$) power spectra, peak counts, minima, one-point PDFs, and Minkowski functionals -- from "Replace" fields against hydrodynamical and DMO simulations. We find that replacing all halos with $M\geq10^{12}\,h^{-1}\,{\rm M}_\odot$ out to $r\leq5R_{200}$ recovers $\sim 90\%$ of the baryonic suppression in $P(k)$ and $C_\ell$ with the remaining $\sim 10\%$ originating from lower-mass halos or material farther outside of DM halos. Each statistic has distinct sensitivities to baryons: $P(k)$ and $C_\ell$ are sensitive to a broad range of masses and radii, whereas WL peaks are primarily affected by the cores of massive halos. We show that BCMs applied to massive halos and calibrated to match hydrodynamical $P(k)$ make two cancelling "mistakes": they underpredict core masses and compensate by overpredicting baryonic impacts at larger radii, thereby explaining previously reported failures of peak statistics in these models. We provide a framework for diagnosing critical mass/radius regions in baryonic modeling for a range of statistics for next-generation BCMs.

AI.tldr: The study reveals limitations of current baryon correction models in weak lensing analyses by showing they partially capture baryonic effects but fail in halo cores, offering a diagnostic framework for better modeling in upcoming surveys.
AI.motivation: Upcoming weak lensing surveys require precise control of systematic effects, particularly baryonic effects that affect matter distribution modeling.
AI.method: Progressively replaced regions around halos of varying masses in dark matter-only simulations with hydrodynamical counterparts; compared multiple statistics from these 'Replace' fields against hydrodynamical and DMO simulations.
AI.result: Replacing halos with masses above 10^{12} solar masses out to 5 times their radius recovers about 90% of baryonic suppression in power spectra; remaining differences stem from lower-mass halos or material beyond halos. Statistics show distinct sensitivities to baryons, and conventional baryon correction models calibrated to power spectra introduce compensating errors in halo core and outer region mass predictions.
AI.conclusion: Current baryon correction models, while effective at matching power spectra, fail to accurately capture baryonic effects in halo cores, causing errors in peak statistics. A framework is provided to identify critical mass and radius ranges for improved baryonic modeling in future studies.

title: Unveiling the biconical geometry of the outflow in the ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 5204 X-1
comment: 14 pages, 14 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) are non-nuclear X-ray binary systems that exceed the Eddington luminosity for a 10 Msun black hole. The majority of these sources are thought to be stellar-mass compact objects accreting at super-Eddington rates, exhibiting powerful relativistic winds. These winds have been identified through the detection of absorption lines with a blueshift as high as 0.3c and emission lines typically found at their laboratory wavelengths. In this work, we analysed the XMM-Newton data of the ULX NGC 5204 X-1, which has been observed to exhibit emission lines with a blueshift of about 0.3c. The aim of this study is to examine the geometry and physical properties of the accretion disc and the relativistic outflows. In addition, we aim to explore the factors that influence the ULX spectral transitions. We undertook an observing campaign with XMM-Newton to explore the source behaviour at different luminosities. In this first paper of the series, we performed high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy, including archival data, with the RGS instrument which allowed us to resolve both emission and absorption lines. The outflows features were characterised using physical models of plasma in collisional-ionisation and photoionisation equilibrium. We identify collisionally-ionised blueshifted and redshifted components at about 0.3c. These findings have high statistical significance and suggest a biconical structure for the outflow. Additionally, the analysis of the O VII line triplet observed in the spectrum enables us to infer physical properties of the low-velocity line-emitting plasma, e.g. electron density (ne $\sim 10^{10}$ cm$^{-3}$) and temperature (Te $ \geq 1.5 \times 10^5$ K). A hybrid plasma whose ionisation balance is affected by both collisions and radiation is favoured.

AI.tldr: The study of NGC 5204 X-1 using XMM-Newton data reveals relativistic biconical outflows at ~0.3c and characterizes the plasma's physical conditions, supporting a hybrid ionisation state influenced by collisions and radiation.
AI.motivation: To better understand the nature and geometry of powerful relativistic winds in ULXs, in particular, NGC 5204 X-1, and to explore factors influencing spectral transitions by analyzing emission and absorption line diagnostics with high-resolution spectroscopy.
AI.method: The study employed high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy using the XMM-Newton RGS instrument, combining new and archival data. Physical plasma models assuming collisional-ionisation and photoionisation equilibrium were applied to characterize emission and absorption lines and infer outflow geometry and plasma properties.
AI.result: This paper investigates the ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 5204 X-1 using high-resolution XMM-Newton RGS spectroscopy to analyze emission and absorption features associated with relativistic winds. It reveals collisionally-ionised blueshifted and redshifted outflows with velocities around 0.3c, suggesting a biconical outflow geometry. The study also derives physical properties of low-velocity plasma via O VII triplet analysis, indicating electron densities of ~10^{10} cm^{-3} and temperatures ≥1.5 × 10^{5} K, with ionisation influenced by both collisional and photoionisation processes.
AI.conclusion: The observed blueshifted and redshifted collisionally-ionised components near 0.3c confirm a biconical outflow structure from the ULX. The O VII triplet analysis constrains the plasma conditions and supports a hybrid plasma ionisation model, advancing understanding of ULX accretion and outflow geometry.

title: Cosmological gravity on all scales V: MCMC forecasts combining large scale structure and CMB lensing for binned phenomenological modified gravity
summary: As cosmology rapidly approaches the data-dominated phase of stage IV large scale structure surveys, the modelling of nonlinear scales has become a serious challenge that faces the community, particularly when analysing models beyond $w$CDM. In this work, we emulate the matter power spectrum in a phenomenological parameterisation of modified gravity in which a time-varying effective gravitational constant $μ$ and a gravitational slip $η$ are binned in redshift. We are able to achieve accuracy $<1\%$ in the modified gravity boost relative to COLA (COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration) simulations. We forecast the constraining power for each bin using a simulated $3\times 2$pt LSST Y10-like data vector and a $6\times 2$pt LSST Y10 x Simons Observatory cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing data vector. We recover the characteristic degeneracy between $μ$ and $η$ previously identified in Fisher forecasts and demonstrate that the best-constrained direction corresponds to the combination $Σ=μ(1+η)/2$ which governs the lensing potential. We show that while large scale structure is sensitive to growth of structure at low redshift, CMB lensing extends the sensitivity to a higher redshift range. These results demonstrate that fast emulation of nonlinear modified-gravity effects enables full Bayesian analyses of model-agnostic gravity parameterisations with realistic survey data vectors and astrophysical systematics.

AI.tldr: This study develops a precise emulator for nonlinear matter power spectrum under time-varying modified gravity parameters, achieving high accuracy and enabling robust Bayesian inference with upcoming LSST and CMB lensing data, highlighting complementary redshift sensitivities and parameter degeneracies.
AI.motivation: The challenge of modeling nonlinear scales in cosmology for large-scale structure surveys, especially beyond the standard $w$CDM framework.
AI.method: Emulation of the matter power spectrum using a phenomenological parameterization of modified gravity with time-varying effective gravitational constant $μ$ and gravitational slip $η$ binned in redshift, calibrated against COLA simulations; forecasting constraints using simulated LSST Y10 and Simons Observatory data vectors.
AI.result: Achieved accuracy better than 1% in modified gravity boost relative to simulations; identified degeneracy between $μ$ and $η$ with best-constrained parameter combination $Σ=μ(1+η)/2$ affecting lensing potential; showed complementary redshift sensitivity between large scale structure and CMB lensing.
AI.conclusion: Fast emulation of nonlinear modified-gravity effects allows full Bayesian analyses of model-agnostic gravity parameterizations using realistic survey data and systematics, enhancing constraint capabilities on modified gravity models with upcoming data.

title: The twin-jet system in the FRII radio galaxy 3C 452: A sub-parsec scale VLBI study
comment: Main: 11 pages, 9 figures. Appendix: 5 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: We present a comprehensive multifrequency VLBI analysis of the FRII, high-excitation radio galaxy 3C 452, aiming to resolve and analyze for the first time its twin-jet structure on sub-parsec scales. Our data set comprises High Sensitivity Array (HSA) observations at 4.9, 8.4, 15.4, 23.6, and 43.2 GHz. Through fitting methods performed in both the visibility and the image plane, we trace the jet expansion from scales of a few thousand to nearly $10^5$ Schwarzschild radii ($R_S$) on both the approaching and receding jets. Additionally, we derive the core brightness temperatures and Doppler factors to constrain the jet's orientation and intrinsic speed. Our study provides the first detailed description of the twin-jet system in 3C 452 on VLBI scales, confirming it as a rare FRII source with jets detected down to millimeter wavelengths. We resolve both jet and counter-jet down to scales of a few thousand $R_S$, revealing a symmetric, parabolically expanding structure with power-law indices $k \approx 0.66$ (jet) and $k \approx 0.47$ (counter-jet). The brightness temperature analysis yields low Doppler factors ($δ\sim 0.03$-$0.83$), indicative of Doppler de-boosting due to the large viewing angle ($θ\approx 70^\circ$) and/or a magnetically dominated jet base. A spectral index analysis reveals a strongly inverted core spectrum ($α> 2$) with additional absorption at the highest frequencies, followed by a sharp steepening ($α\sim -2.5$) to optically thin values in the innermost jet. Finally, a comparison between broad- and narrow-line high-excitation radio galaxies shows that jets in narrow-line sources such as 3C 452 and Cygnus A complete collimation at $\leq 10^5 R_S$, whereas broad-line sources exhibit shape transitions at $10^6$-$10^7 R_S$, suggesting that orientation plays an important role in the observed collimation scales.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first detailed VLBI analysis of 3C 452's twin jets across multiple frequencies, revealing symmetric parabolic expansion, low Doppler factors due to large viewing angles, and a strongly inverted core spectrum; it concludes that jet collimation scales differ by source type and orientation effects.
AI.motivation: To resolve and analyze the twin-jet structure of the FRII high-excitation radio galaxy 3C 452 on sub-parsec scales for the first time using multifrequency VLBI data.
AI.method: Comprehensive multifrequency VLBI observations with the High Sensitivity Array at 4.9, 8.4, 15.4, 23.6, and 43.2 GHz; data analysis includes fitting in visibility and image planes to trace jet expansion from a few thousand to nearly 10^5 Schwarzschild radii, along with brightness temperature and Doppler factor derivations.
AI.result: Resolved both jet and counter-jet down to a few thousand Schwarzschild radii, revealing symmetric parabolic expansion with specific power-law indices; low Doppler factors consistent with Doppler de-boosting and large viewing angles; identification of a strongly inverted core spectrum with absorption and steepening to optically thin emission in the innermost jet; found that jet collimation scales differ between narrow- and broad-line high-excitation radio galaxies, implicating orientation effects.
AI.conclusion: The study provides the first detailed VLBI-scale description of the twin-jet system in 3C 452, confirming it as a rare FRII source with jets detectable at millimeter wavelengths, exhibiting symmetric parabolic expansion, and showing that orientation significantly influences jet collimation scales in high-excitation radio galaxies.

title: Sensitivity to Axion-like Particle dark matter with very-high-energy gamma-ray observations of Active Galactic Nuclei located behind Galaxy Clusters
summary:
Axion-Like-Particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudo-scalar particles actively searched as light dark matter candidates. The coupling of ALPs to photons can give rise to distinctive spectral features in the observed gamma-ray spectrum of astrophysical sources.
  We perform a forecast study on the sensitivity to ALP-photon interactions using stacked mock observations of selected active galactic nuclei (AGNs) located behind galaxy clusters (GC). The ALP-photon conversion in the magnetic fields of galaxy clusters give rise to absorption-like features in AGN spectra that are subject to large variance in their prediction for individual sources. We consider here a stacking analysis of multiple AGN-cluster pairs, which yields a more controlled prediction of the expected ALP-induced spectral patterns in the observed gamma-ray spectra.
  Using realistic mock observations of selected Fermi-LAT AGNs by ongoing Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes such as H.E.S.S., MAGIC and VERITAS, we provide a careful assessment of the expected sensitivity of a combined statistical analysis of many AGN-GC pairs, together with the impact of modelling and instrumental uncertainties. The sensitivity reaches ALP-photon couplings down to 6$\times$10$^{-13}$ GeV$^{-1}$ for an ALP mass of 3$\times$10$^{-8}$ eV, and is currently statistically dominated indicating further improvements from more observations. Such a stacking analysis approach enables exploration of the yet-uncharted ALP dark matter parameter space in the 10$^{-8}$ - 10$^{-7}$ eV mass range.

AI.tldr: The study forecasts that stacking gamma-ray observations of AGNs behind galaxy clusters can sensitively detect ALP-photon interactions, enabling exploration of an uncharted ALP dark matter mass range with current and future telescopes.
AI.motivation: To explore the potential of using gamma-ray spectral features from active galactic nuclei (AGNs) behind galaxy clusters for detecting Axion-Like-Particles (ALPs), which are candidate light dark matter particles, due to their coupling with photons.
AI.method: Performed a forecast sensitivity study using stacked mock observations of multiple AGN-galaxy cluster pairs, employing realistic simulations based on data from Fermi-LAT AGNs and atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS). The approach considers ALP-photon conversion in galaxy cluster magnetic fields and accounts for modelling and instrumental uncertainties.
AI.result: Demonstrated that a combined statistical stacking analysis of many AGN-GC pairs can reach ALP-photon coupling sensitivities down to 6×10^{-13} GeV^{-1} for an ALP mass of 3×10^{-8} eV, with the current sensitivity limited by statistical uncertainties and promising for improvement with additional observations.
AI.conclusion: Stacking analyses of gamma-ray spectra from multiple AGN-cluster pairs provide a robust method to probe previously unexplored ALP dark matter parameter space in the mass range 10^{-8} - 10^{-7} eV, opening new avenues for ALP detection efforts.

title: Scale-Dependent Loop Corrections to the Inflationary Power Spectrum
summary: Loop corrections to primordial correlation functions are unavoidable due to the non-linear nature of gravity. Previous works have established a robust framework for computing the renormalised one-loop power spectra of scalar and tensor modes, but primarily in (near) de Sitter backgrounds. In this work, we develop a consistent renormalisation procedure applicable to inflationary backgrounds that strongly break de Sitter symmetries and generate scale-dependent features in the primordial spectra. Our analysis is performed within the Effective Field Theory (EFT) of inflationary fluctuations, allowing for arbitrary time dependence of the Wilson coefficients. We show that both ultraviolet divergences and tadpoles of the theory, despite their strong time and scale dependence, can be cancelled by a finite set of local counter-terms compatible with the EFT symmetries. Importantly, this result only relies on the existence of an initial phase of adiabatic evolution continuously related to the Bunch-Davies vacuum and holds independently of the precise time dependence of the background and of the free-field mode functions. We then study two concrete realisations, corresponding to resonant and sharp features. In both cases, all calculations are carried out exactly in the limit of small feature amplitude. We analyse perturbativity and provide the first explicit demonstration that the renormalised one-loop power spectrum generated by a localised feature along the inflationary trajectory vanishes both at large and small scales. Our scale-dependent renormalisation framework implies that models of primordial features used to fit CMB residuals are consistent with perturbativity bounds, and opens the door to systematic studies of loop corrections in more complicated scenarios relevant for scalar-induced gravitational waves and primordial black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a consistent renormalisation framework for inflationary models with strong scale-dependent features, proving loop corrections are well-controlled and consistent with perturbation theory, thereby validating feature models and enabling study of loop effects in complex inflationary scenarios.
AI.motivation: Existing renormalisation frameworks for loop corrections in inflation predominantly assume near de Sitter symmetry, limiting their applicability. To address scenarios with strong breaking of these symmetries producing scale-dependent primordial features, a more general renormalisation procedure is needed to ensure theoretical consistency and perturbativity of loop corrections in realistic inflationary models.
AI.method: Employing the EFT of inflationary fluctuations with time-dependent Wilson coefficients, the authors implement a renormalisation scheme that cancels UV divergences and tadpoles through local counter-terms. They test the framework on resonant and sharp feature models by performing exact calculations in the limit of small feature amplitude, verifying perturbativity and scale-dependent behavior of the loop-corrected spectra.
AI.result: The paper develops a general renormalisation procedure for one-loop corrections to primordial power spectra within the EFT of inflation, applicable beyond near-de Sitter backgrounds and accommodating strong time-dependent features. It proves that UV divergences and tadpoles can be canceled by a finite set of local counter-terms consistent with EFT symmetries, relying only on an initial adiabatic phase. Applications to resonant and sharp feature models show perturbativity and demonstrate vanishing loop corrections at large and small scales, supporting the theoretical consistency of feature models used in CMB analyses and enabling further loop correction studies in scenarios relevant to gravitational waves and primordial black holes.
AI.conclusion: A finite set of local counter-terms suffices to cancel all UV divergences and tadpoles in inflationary EFT with scale-dependent features, ensuring perturbative consistency of loop-corrected power spectra. Loop corrections from localized features vanish at extreme scales, supporting the phenomenological use of such models and paving the way for loop studies in related cosmological phenomena.

title: X-ray evidence from NuSTAR for a Mach 3 shock in Merging Galaxy Cluster ZWCL 1856.8
comment: 15 Pages, 9 Figures, 2 Tables. Revision submitted to ApJ
summary: We present spectral analysis results of deeper (270 ks) NuSTAR observations of the merging galaxy cluster system, ZWCL1856.8+6616, at redshift z=0.304, following a pilot study using shallower (30 ks) NuSTAR data (Tumer et al. 2024). The cluster hosts a double radio relic, pointing to a similar mass head-on collision at/near the plane of sky. We aim to find the relation between radio and X-ray shock features. Using data from both focal plane modules of NuSTAR, we study the temperature structure across the field of view and report on the X-ray detected shock strength at the relic sites. We generate nominal and cross-ARFs with nucrossarf to disentangle photon cross-contamination within regions of interest due to the moderate point spread function of NuSTAR. Here we report one of the strongest X-ray detected shocks in a galaxy cluster merger with M=3.90(+1.64,-0.85) at the Northern relic site, that is unprecedentedly larger than the radio counterpart; M=2.5+/-0.2 (Jones et al. 2021a), and we report Southern shock strength as M=2.36(+0.58,-0.46). We argue that since the Northern relic (or radio shock), is confined in a very small region in the sky, particle acceleration is more efficient and is likely to grow in the post-shock regions. In addition, we search for inverse Compton (IC) emission at the radio relic sites; however, an IC component was not detected.

AI.tldr: This paper presents deep NuSTAR X-ray observations of galaxy cluster ZWCL1856.8+6616, analyzing shock features related to its double radio relics from a merging event.
AI.motivation: To understand the relationship between radio and X-ray shock features in a merging galaxy cluster, especially clarifying differences in shock strength and particle acceleration mechanisms.
AI.method: Deep NuSTAR observations (270 ks) were used to map temperature structures and measure shock strengths by addressing photon cross-contamination through customized response files. Shock Mach numbers were derived from spectral analysis at relic locations.
AI.result: A very strong Northern shock with M=3.90(+1.64,-0.85) was found, significantly exceeding the radio Mach number of 2.5±0.2; the Southern shock was measured at M=2.36(+0.58,-0.46). No inverse Compton emission was detected at the relic sites.
AI.conclusion: The study reports exceptionally strong X-ray detected shocks at the relic sites, with the Northern shock showing a higher Mach number than its radio counterpart, indicating efficient particle acceleration in localized regions. No inverse Compton emission was detected.
